messages:
alesha: Hey folks — Zenora (prospect) just returned their vendor risk form. Primary asks: full subprocessor list, KMS key residency, and confirmation of SOC2 scope covering production inference and logging. They also want an example dataflow diagram and statement on retention windows.

david: Thanks. Can you paste the specific questions or attach the PDF? I can draft answers for KMS and encryption. Out until 11:30 PT but will take this after.

alesha: Pasting the excerpt they highlighted:
> 1) List of subprocessors and locations
> 2) Where are KMS keys stored (region) and who manages them
> 3) Is SOC2 Type II coverage applicable to inference endpoints and logs?
> 4) Data retention defaults and how to change for enterprise customers
> 5) Any cross-border transfers and subprocessors outside EEA/US

lia: Quick notes:
- Subprocessors: analytics (Amplitude) in US, error/telemetry (Sentry) US, cloud infra (GCP/AWS) multiple regions, hosted model vendor (third-party cache) — need to pull canonical list from infra-team.
- KMS: We offer customer-managed keys for Private, and for Hosted keys are in our cloud KMS in the region of the deployment. Need to confirm exact region names.

mike: For SOC2: our current scope includes production inference and a subset of logs (access logs, syslogs) but redact user-provided content from monitoring pipelines. We should avoid novel wording — I'll pull the SOC2 control mapping doc and paste a short line.

alesha: Good. Zenora asked if we can give a redacted dataflow diagram. I sketched one — small PNG attached in reply to customer but they asked for inline. Lia, can you quickly export a simplified ASCII diagram we can share?

lia: Sure — here you go:

```
Client -> Redwood API (frontend LB)
  -> Auth service (token validation)
  -> Inference runtime (GPU pool)
    -> KV cache (redis, optional)
    -> Model artifacts (object store)
  -> Logging (redacted traces) -> Obs datastore (limited retention)
```

lia: Note: keys used for model artifacts are KMS-wrapped; we store only wrapped keys unless customer uses CMK.

david: Draft answers for the customer (short bullets) — please review: 
- Subprocessors: see attached canonical list and locations (US, EU, APAC).
- KMS: Hosted keys stored in region of deployment in cloud KMS (we can provide key alias and region). For Redwood Private customers we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS).
- SOC2: Yes — SOC2 Type II report covers production inference and operational logging; we exclude plaintext customer data in monitoring. We can provide an SOC2 letter under NDA.
- Retention: Default inference logs retained 30 days; request longer retention via contract and we can provide per-route retention settings.
- Cross-border: Some subprocessors operate outside EEA/US; we provide SCCs where applicable and list subprocessors in our standard DPA.

mike: Edits: change "we can provide an SOC2 letter" -> "we can provide a SOC2 attestation under NDA and an SOC2 summary for sales team". Also add that access to raw request content is restricted to platform SRE on a need-to-know basis and requires approved ops tickets.

alesha: Great. Action items: 1) Lia to export full subprocessors CSV (infra owner) — can you get by EOD? 2) David to create the redacted SOC2 attestation request template for NDA send. 3) Mike to confirm exact retention policy text. 4) I'll send the draft to Zenora CISO with the ASCII diagram and invite them to an hour Q&A.

onboarding-bot: Reminder: attach DPA link (https://redwood.example/dpa) and use template DPA v3.2 for Zenora.

lia: I'll have the subprocessors CSV by 5pm PT and will include region fields.

david: I'll draft the attestation email + NDA language and ping legal if needed.

mike: I'll paste the retention policy snippet here in 30m.

alesha: Thanks team — keeping this tight, Zenora is on an onboarding timeline for next month and wants answers before their security review on the 18th. I'll update the thread after I send the doc to them. :thumbsup:
